chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Yunus, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Every mature person, whether male or female, who accuses a child or an adult, male or female, Muslim or non-Muslim, free or slave, upon him is the full penalty of accusation (hadd al-fariyah), and upon the non-mature person is the disciplinary penalty (hadd al-adab).

As for what the beginning of this report included regarding the obligation of the full penalty upon one who accuses a child, it is to be understood as referring to one who accuses him of the lineage of adultery to one of his parents, by saying 'O son of the fornicator' or 'the fornicatress', or 'Your mother/father fornicated with you', because that obligates the full penalty upon him.

As for if he accuses him with an accusation that does not extend to one of the two parents, then the full penalty is not obligatory upon him, but rather he is subject to disciplinary punishment (ta'zir).
This is indicated by what we have previously mentioned from the earlier reports and what we have cited in the book Tahdhib al-Ahkam.

As for what the report included regarding the obligation of the full penalty upon one who accuses a disbeliever, or a Jew, or a Christian, it is possible that the intended meaning is if his mother is Muslim, then the full penalty is obligatory upon one who accuses him due to the sanctity of the Muslim woman.
If it is not so, then only disciplinary punishment is obligatory, according to what we have previously mentioned.

It is also possible that the mention of 'hadd' (penalty) in the report refers to 'ta'zir' (disciplinary punishment) in both cases, even though the term 'hadd al-fariyah' is used for it, because that is also deserved by accusation, even if it is not a full hadd.

key_terms.حَدّ الْفِرْيَةِ: Full statutory penalty for false accusation of adultery

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the full penalty and disciplinary punishment for accusing a child of adultery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi elucidates the distinction between the full statutory penalty (hadd) and discretionary punishment (ta'zir) in cases of false accusation (qadhf) against children, specifically noting that the hadd applies when the accusation implies lineage corruption involving a parent. The text further explores the juristic debate regarding non-Muslims, suggesting that the hadd may apply if their mother is Muslim, or that the term 'hadd' is used broadly to include ta'zir in other contexts. This reflects the Shia scholarly approach to contextualizing legal terminology within the specific social and familial structures of the time.
